    StartersEat me cakesLittle butter cakes with white icingHow to make it125g butter, softened125g caster sugar2 eggs125g self-raising flour200g icing sugar2 tbsp waterpink food colouring, a few dropsBeat the butter and sugar until pale and creamy.Beat in the eggs one at a time, then fold in the flour.Spoon into a greased mini muffin tin and bake at 175°C until risen and golden.Cool the cakes on a wire rack.Mix the icing sugar with the water until thick, then ice the cakes white. Tint a little icing pink and pipe EAT ME on top.MainsCroquet lawn chicken and leek pieChicken thigh and leek pie in a creamy thyme sauceHow to make it800g chicken thighs, diced2 tbsp olive oil2 leeks, sliced1 tbsp plain flour250ml chicken stock200ml thickened cream4 sprigs of thyme1 sheet puff pastry (or 2 for a deeper lid)salt and pepper, to tasteBrown the chicken in the oil in batches, seasoning with salt and pepper, then set aside. Slice the leeks.Soften the leeks in the same pan.Stir in the flour, then the stock, cream and thyme. Return the chicken and simmer until thick.Pour into a pie dish and top with the pastry, pressing the edges down.Bake at 200°C until puffed and deep golden.Mad Hatter's tea party finger sandwichesThe Mad Hatter's long tea tableHow to make itAs written, serves 4Three kinds of crustless finger sandwiches, cucumber and cream cheese, egg and cress, and ham and mustard, stacked high on tiered plates.Boil 4 eggs for 10 minutes, cool, peel and mash with 3 tbsp mayo and salt.Mix 150g cream cheese with chopped dill.Spread 12 slices of soft white bread with butter.Make 2 rounds of thin cucumber and cream cheese, 2 of egg and cress, and 2 of ham and mustard, using 150g ham.Trim the crusts and cut each round into 3 fingers.Stack on tiered plates.SweetsTea party cakeVanilla sponge sandwiched with strawberry jam, iced in pastel coloursHow to make it250g butter, softened250g caster sugar4 eggs250g self-raising flour120g strawberry jam300g icing sugar3 tbsp milkpastel food colouring, a few drops8 birthday candlesBeat the butter and sugar until pale, add the eggs one at a time, then fold in the flour.Divide between 2 lined tins and bake at 175°C until a skewer comes out clean.Cool the cakes completely in the tins, then turn out.Mix the icing sugar with the milk and tint in pastel colours.Sandwich the cakes with jam, ice in pastel colours and add the candles.Queen of Hearts tartsPuff pastry hearts filled with strawberry jam and whipped creamHow to make it2 sheets of puff pastry, thawed120g strawberry jam300ml thickened cream2 tbsp icing sugarCut hearts from the pastry sheets and lay them on lined trays.Bake at 200°C until puffed and golden.Cool completely on a rack.Whip the cream to soft peaks.Split each heart in half, fill with jam and cream, then dust the tops with icing sugar.DrinksDrink me iced earl grey lemonadeEarl Grey tea with honey and lemonade, over iceHow to make it4 earl grey tea bags500ml boiling water1 tbsp honey500ml lemonade1 lemon4 cups iceSteep the tea bags in the boiling water, stir in the honey and remove the bags.Cool the tea, then chill if you have time.Mix the tea with the lemonade and a squeeze of lemon.Pour over ice in mismatched teacups.
